speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Hence, I think it is important that all potential adoptive parents undergo comprehensive medical examinations certifying that they are fit and healthy, both physically and mentally.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I look forward to the Minister's clarification on this issue.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Next, I would like to express my concerns about the threshold for the dispensation of the unfit, biological parents' consent for their children to be adopted.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This group of parents would include those who are in jail for extended periods of time, are very abusive or drug addicts and so on.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I fully understand and support the Ministry's review on this issue and its aim to enable affected children to grow up in safe and stable families.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Severance of ties between the biological parents and their children should only be allowed under strict conditions and must be very carefully considered.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I seek the Ministry's assurance in this sensitive matter that the best interests of the child will be considered thoroughly from all angles.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The disclosure of a child's adoption is a very sensitive and emotional issue.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Depending on the relationships and personalities of adoptive parents and children, the consequences can vary widely.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Sometimes, the disclosure can destroy an established relationship.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: When the adopted child has become an adult and wishes to find out who his or her natural parents are, that is his or her choice.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For younger children, it should be left as a private matter between the adoptive parents and the adopted child.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I hope that the Ministry will continue to adopt a cautious approach, as it has done so far.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: Through the work they do, I have come to understand some of the legal and administrative challenges posed in adoption in their nation's context, especially in ensuring that children are safe and valued.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: Ultimately, the laws surrounding adoption should exist to find the best family for the child and not the best child for families.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: The Adoption of Children Bill strikes a good balance in placing safeguards for adopted children to be placed in a healthy family environment, while also reducing obstacles from them being placed in healthy families sooner.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: I am excited at the many lives this Bill will change, not only for our children and families, but the impact this will have on our community and nation.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: As we speak of the Bill today, may I propose to the House, and fellow Singaporeans, to respectfully consider adoption as a real and viable option to starting and growing families, alongside assisted reproduction schemes.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: UNICEF estimates 15 million orphans who have lost both parents in the world, also known as double orphans, the majority of who are in Asia.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: However, double orphans are not the only pool of children that need to find a home.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: We have children whose parents fail to perform parental duties for various reasons, also known as social orphans, many of whom are under state and institutional care.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: There is no shortage of physical and social orphans locally and overseas who are needing, if not, longing for healthy families.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: There is much that can still be done to raise awareness and to open the hearts and minds in Singapore to the idea of adoption.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: In comparison, the demand for Assisted Reproduction Technology (ART) procedures has surged, evidenced by a 40% increase in the take up of funding for ART procedures between 2015 and 2019.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: Such demand has also led to recent policy changes in assisted reproduction; such as raising the age limit for those undergoing ART procedures, as well as increased co-funding for such procedures.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: These measures have been most welcomed, and many residents and friends I know are grateful for these changes that support their growing family.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: However parenthood comes to us, it is a miracle.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: I sincerely look forward to the day where demand for both ART procedures and adoption will be on par, and to see more families embracing adoption as part of starting and building families.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: Perhaps in the near future, similar assistance used in supporting ART can also be provided to adopting families who pass the Adoption Suitability Assessment (ASA).

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: Adoption shows us that we do not have to look like the other person to love them.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: It expands the social and emotional capacity of a people and society.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: When a child knows that he or she has been chosen by a family to be loved and is given a safe home and life resources to explore new possibilities, it transforms his or her life in a manner that impacts generations to come.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: Adopted at the age of 12 after his father passed away, Mr Nelson Mandela was the first in his family to receive formal education, alongside the children of his adoptive father.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: Because of the education opportunities accorded by his adoptive family, he became politically active during his university years and beyond and never imagined that he would be responsible in leading a nation out of apartheid, radically changing the lives of South Africans.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: Closer to home, someone, whom I have deep respect for, chose to adopt her two children: her first, a daughter from China; and her second, a son from a teenager here who decided to release her baby for adoption over abortion.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: Both children are well-loved and cared for and have grown to be confident and contributing Singaporeans.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: As a matter of fact, her son today is a grateful recipient of a scholarship in a vocation of his dream.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: What a difference adoption has made to the lives of these young people and a joy they have been to their family!

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: Abandonment does not have to be the destiny of orphaned children, but an opportunity for families with emotional and financial capacity to help the children discover their destiny, no matter what age they come into their homes.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: While children's homes could still give them the best quality of life possible, there is so much more a family brings to a child.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: Studies show that being raised in an institutional environment contributes substantially to the delayed and adverse development of young children.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: Studies also feature that poor development is not associated with selected gene pool nor adverse pre-institutional experience; but when placed in families, most of such children display substantial catch-up growth, beginning soon after adoption, across physical, mental and social domains.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: By placing orphaned children in families, we support them to see beyond their circumstances, uplift them to greater things.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: It gives our children courage to pursue all that life has for them; and to know that they have a destiny to fulfil.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: With this, Mr Deputy Speaker, I support this Bill.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: First, I would like to ask the Ministry if it would provide more details about checks on the children, post-adoption.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The checks and screening before adoption are quite stringent, but what about after adoption?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Such checks would also be opportunities for social workers to find out if the adoptive parents need support in specific areas and, thus, refer them to the appropriate support programmes or groups.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Second, would the Minister share how the adoptive parents would be prepared and supported in the area of disclosure?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: What kind of guidelines and at which age for the child would the parents be advised?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It is natural for anyone to want to discover more about his or her own roots.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: For some, knowing who their birth parents are and why they were given up for adoption helps to provide them some closure.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: (In Mandarin):   I would like to ask MSF, in the first two to three years after adoption, whether it will send social workers to do home interviews to check on the condition of these children.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This will enable the social workers to understand how the adoptive parents are coping and, when necessary, refer them to support programmes and groups.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Next, would the Minister share how the Ministry's briefing is going to teach adoptive parents how to disclose to the children that they are adopted?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Lastly, there will be some who are adopted, who want to understand more about their birth parents and the circumstances of their adoption.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I am glad that we share the same view that, ultimately, the child's welfare must be our starting point and is at the heart of adoption.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We have heard many views and suggestions on ways we can strengthen our current adoption framework and processes.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: First of all, the Bill covers the entire adoption process and proceedings in Singapore, regardless of a child's nationality.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This is in reply to Mr Yip Hon Weng's query on whether the Bill applies to foreign children identified for adoption.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Several Members spoke about the proposed changes to the eligibility criteria for prospective adopters.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Seah Kian Peng asked whether residency requirements should be further tightened to disallow joint applications where both applicants are Singapore Permanent Residents (PRs).

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: PRs form an integral part of Singapore society.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: A good number have committed to making Singapore their home and taking up permanent residency is one step on their journey towards citizenship.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As I shared in my opening speech, the number of children in Singapore available for adoption is limited.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Hence, we would prioritise adopters with a stronger nexus to Singapore, who must qualify for the physical residency criteria, too.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: However, we may not wish to take this principle too far, such as to disqualify applicants based on their degree of connection to Singapore alone.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Some Members asked about the scope of the provision to bar applicants who have committed serious crimes from adopting.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will also reference established frameworks that list serious offences.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Depending on the types of cases that surface over time, we may review this list.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For offences not in the prescribed list, the applicants' criminal record will still be taken into account as part of the Adoption Suitability Assessment (ASA) by authorised adoption agencies, the Guardian-in-Adoption's (GIA) recommendations and when the Court considers the specific application.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: GIA will look at each case holistically and balance various considerations.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This includes the applicant's relationship with the child, the availability of alternate caregivers for the child if an adoption order is not granted and how long the applicant has remained crime-free.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The longer the person has remained crime-free, the more favourably it would present his or her application.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng also asked whether the provision covers offences committed abroad and offences committed by applicants' immediate family members.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: While we will only prescribe offences under Singapore law, offences of a similar nature committed overseas will be considered in assessing their suitability.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Today, holistic assessments of the suitability of the applicants' household includes consideration of the other household members' background.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I will now move on to Mr Seah Kian Peng's comment relating to public policies.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: He asked what happens if a single applicant applies to adopt and, subsequently, marries someone of the same gender overseas.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Even if it were to happen, we should not pronounce on how a Court will, ultimately, decide on the case.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It suffices to say that the Court has ruled that public policies are relevant and will be considered in any specific application and that the Government has made clear our public policy on this.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As I have mentioned in my opening speech, the Government does not encourage planned and deliberate single parenthood as a lifestyle choice.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Singapore's public policy continues to be one which encourages parenthood within marriage.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We also do not support the formation of same-sex family units through institutions and processes like adoption.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: These public policies will continue to guide suitability assessments.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This Bill also clarifies the duty of the applicant to provide accurate information and to update the information provided if circumstances change.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I will now address Members' queries on suitability assessments.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Some, like Mr Dennis Tan, have asked how ASA differs from the pre-adoption assessment known as the Home Study Report (HSR) today, in particular, whether more information will be required from prospective adopters.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In this regard, Mr Seah Kian Peng suggested requiring prospective adopters to provide character referees and periodic declarations of their circumstances.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: HSR done today is a comprehensive assessment of the suitability of the applicants and the living environment that they would provide the child if the adoption were to be granted.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: ASA will continue to cover all key aspects covered by HSR.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It will continue to be rigorous and assessed by qualified and trained professionals.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The four social service agencies that perform HSR today will be authorised to conduct ASAs.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In such cases, the child is likely to already be living with the prospective adopters at the point of assessment.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Thus, in such cases, the information required will be tailored to the specific child.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Assessors will consider the actual dynamics of the relationship between the prospective adopters and the child and their understanding of the child's needs.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: On character referees, MSF already requires prospective adopters to provide them today.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Today, the Court-appointed GIA checks in regularly with applicants on their circumstances.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This ensures that assessments are up to date.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Louis Ng asked about the prerequisites to obtain a favourable ASA, guidelines on the new processes and the circumstances under which a simplified ASA may be issued.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We have legislated and will also prescribe factors that assessors must consider in determining suitability.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Relevant factors include the ability to provide a safe and suitable home environment for the child and marital stability.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: MSF will provide more information to assist prospective adopters and other key stakeholders when transiting to the new processes.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This would include authorised adoption agencies that they can approach for assistance during their adoption journey.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The adoption process can be shortened if prospective adopters provide all necessary information to assessors in a timely manner.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim asked about streamlining GIA's investigations by relying on ASA findings.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Such findings by authorised adoption agencies will be taken into account by GIA in assessing the case.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: At the same time, some Members have also proposed for more types of checks or assessments to be carried out.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Hence, the issue is about striking the right balance and not to rush through the adoption process.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For example, this could be in a case where an applicant is adopting his step-child with his wife and both of them are able to provide a safe and stable home for the child.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng commented that the relationship between a child identified for adoption and the rest of the family should be considered as part of the assessment.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This is to ascertain if the family is prepared and understands the implications of adoption.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Today, part of the suitability assessment includes interviewing household members, such as other children of prospective adopters, to learn their views.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Louis Ng, Mr Dennis Tan and Ms Ng Ling Ling asked about the cost of ASAs.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Ms Ng Ling Ling further asked about the cost of raising the child after adoption is formalised.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Adopting and raising a child are a life-long commitment and responsibility.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Assessors will look at the prospective adopters' mental, emotional and financial preparedness to adopt.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: ASAs are conducted by social service agencies (SSAs) which charge fees to cover their costs in conducting the assessments.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Adoption is, ultimately, about the welfare of the child.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: If the prospective adopters are not able to cope well with caring for the child in financial, emotional or other terms, that is something that should be of concern to us.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Ms Denise Phua asked how the child's voice would be sought.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As the child's welfare must be a key priority behind every adoption, MSF has already been seeking the child's views and wishes, in relation to his or her proposed adoption today.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Next, I will address Members' queries on medical and mental health assessments for children and prospective adopters.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked if medical and mental health assessments are mandatory for children identified for adoption before proceedings are finalised.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Mark Chay also asked if the child's medical, mental and emotional status is evaluated.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: However, GIA, authorised adoption agencies or the Court may require the child to be assessed if they are of the view that such assessments may be useful to understand or document the child's needs.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh suggested that potential adopters should undergo comprehensive medical examinations, as they tend to be older.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Today, MSF already requires all prospective adopters to undergo health examinations and submit medical reports.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As the adoption process takes time, we also check if the reports are updated.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I will now address Mr Christopher de Souza's suggestion on matching prospective adopters with women with unplanned pregnancies who wish to place their child for adoption.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Today, pregnant women and prospective adopters can approach adoption agencies to indicate that they wish to place their child for adoption and to be matched with a child to adopt, respectively.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Where such women have approached MSF for assistance, we also link them up with the SSAs which can do the matching.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Going forward, MSF is also considering developing a registry to match children in state care with prospective adopters.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I will now move to the issue of disclosing to a child that he or she is adopted.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Ms Joan Pereira asked how we will support adoptive parents with disclosure and what guidelines would be given.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: While there is no universally appropriate age for disclosure, the professionals recommend introducing and normalising the concept of adoption as early as possible.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Beyond the Disclosure Briefing, if at any time prospective adopters or adoptive parents require more assistance with disclosure, they can approach MSF or any authorised adoption agency.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will direct them to relevant support services or support groups, which I will elaborate on subsequently.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Ms Joan Pereira also asked how adopted children who wish to find out more about their birth family can do so and whether MSF will establish an adoption register.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As Mr Gan Thiam Poh said, disclosure is very sensitive for the different parties involved: the child, the adoptive parents and the birth parents.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This also came out very clearly in the consultation process.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: All adoptive parents would, generally, be aware of the identities of their adopted child's birth parents, as a copy of the child's original birth certificate must be submitted to the Courts as part of the adoption application.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Hence, adoptive parents can be the first port of call if their adopted children wish to contact their birth parents.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Some adopted individuals also approach MSF and we assist as far as possible.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Where we are able to contact the birth parents, we will explore whether they would be open to being contacted by the adopted child.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We also work with the adopted child to prepare him or her for possible scenarios.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Sometimes, the birth parents may have passed away or they may be unwilling to establish contact with the child for their own reasons.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Many Members, such as Mr Christopher de Souza, spoke up on supporting prospective adopters and adoptive families through their journey.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: First, the Pre-adoption Briefing provides prospective adopters with an overview of what they can expect during the adoption process.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: ASA then builds on this as assessors interact closely with prospective adopters to address their concerns or queries.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Similarly, once the adoption application is made, GIA will continue to work with prospective adopters.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This includes referring them to relevant support services.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: While ASA and GIA investigations are primarily suitability assessments, they also serve as useful opportunities for prospective adopters to gauge their readiness to undergo the adoption journey.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked if the matters covered in the Pre-Adoption Briefing would be adequate to prepare prospective adopters.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: He also asked about the support measures that are available in cases where there may be compatibility issues between the adoptive parents and the adopted child.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As I shared earlier, the Pre-Adoption Briefing is part of the process of preparation to adopt.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Beyond the mandatory briefings and assessments, prospective adopters and adoptive parents can also tap on formal and informal support groups to support them during their adoption journey – as mentioned by Mr Dennis Tan.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: MSF can also connect them with Family Service Centres (FSCs) for support on issues common to families, such as parent-child conflict or marital stress.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Don Wee suggested providing funding for support groups.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Today, some SSAs organise formal support group sessions covering various topics, including addressing prospective adopters' concerns on disclosure, on a cost-recovery basis.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The SSAs also organise group outings for adoptive families to be introduced to and interact with one another.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Through such sessions, online forums and word-of-mouth, adoptive parents and their adopted children have also formed their own informal support networks.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Louis Ng asked how we will continue to ensure applicants' suitability after an order is made.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Don Wee and Ms Joan Pereira asked whether post-adoption reviews will be mandated at specific milestones.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The Government, therefore, does not interfere in the family unless we have cause for concern.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: MSF also received mixed feedback on such post-adoption reviews during our stakeholder consultations, with some commenting that such reviews are invasive for adoptive parents when similar requirements are not imposed on birth parents.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We note that Assoc Prof Jamus Lim shared similar views on this issue.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Ms Ng Ling Ling suggested that MSF consider providing support services to adopted children up to 21 years old, on a needs basis.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Such orders can be made till the adopted child turns 21, as needed.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Ms Ng Ling Ling also asked if we will introduce support services for adopted children whose adoptive parents decide to undergo divorce and the criteria that the Court may use in determining custody matters for such children.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The Women's Charter provides guidance to the Courts in determining custody matters.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: If adoptive parents, unfortunately, have to contemplate divorce, these same principles apply.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The support services that are given to all divorcing couples with children are also available and extended to adopted children.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Several Members of Parliament, such as Mr Gan Thiam Poh, expressed that dispensation with a birth parent's consent to adoption should only be allowed under very strict conditions.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Louis Ng also asked for more information on how the grounds for such dispensation are determined.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We have calibrated the grounds for dispensation by balancing these two considerations.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Ultimately, it is the Court that will decide whether to dispense with consent, taking into account the case-specific facts and GIA's recommendations.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: To Mr Melvin Yong's query, our intent is to build upon prevailing case law to give more guidance on when dispensation of consent would be in the child's welfare.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Specific to children in state care, Mr Henry Kwek and Mr Yip Hon Weng asked how MSF decides when to pursue adoption for such children instead of fostering or other care options.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Mark Chay asked if there would be opportunities for birth parents to reconcile with their children.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: When a child is removed from his or her parents due to care or protection concerns, they are placed in foster care or in children's homes to provide the care and safety that their homes of origin are not able to provide.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Once the child's immediate safety has been assured, MSF works with the child's birth family to resolve the problematic circumstances, so that the child can return home as soon as possible.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This entails collaborating with them on safety plans and trying to address safety concerns.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We also share with them the plans that we will put in place for the child's welfare should they not be able to resolve these safety concerns.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Officers from the Child Protective Service use an evidence-based Structured Decision-Making framework and consultations with an independent panel of professionals to guide their decision-making.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In some cases, birth families may be unable or unwilling to resolve safety concerns, despite extensive and prolonged assistance from professionals.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In such cases, rather than leaving the child in long-term state care, adoption is a permanency option which would give the child more stability, certainty and a better outcome in life.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Hence, it is only at the point where reunification seems unlikely that we look at facilitating the adoption of that child and cease efforts at reunification.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Should unhappy birth parents harass prospective adopters, our existing laws on protection against harassment will accord them protection.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I will now move on to Members' queries relating to adoption agencies.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Louis Ng and Ms Denise Phua spoke about the accreditation of adoption agencies.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim suggested developing a registry of agencies.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Our approach is to focus on the criminalisation of undesirable adoption practices.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will keep a close watch on the impact of the Bill on adoption agencies' practices and we are prepared to consider further measures in the future, if necessary.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Melvin Yong queried about the number of cases where children identified for adoption were offered to prospective adopters willing to pay the most.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: However, we have heard of such practices and the Bill seeks to introduce measures to deter children from being commodified.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Louis Ng also asked about the mechanism to ensure adoption-related payments are published and declared.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: When applying to Court, all applicants must list every payment they have made or received for adoption-related matters.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: GIA will cross-reference these payments against the figures published by adoption agencies.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Where they do not tally, GIA and authorised officers will investigate further to determine if an offence has been committed.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Ms Denise Phua asked about guidelines for adoption fees.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This depends on the services that the agency provides to prospective adopters and could vary, depending on factors, such as whether the child identified to be adopted is local or foreign.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In this Bill, we have focused on regulating payment categories rather than payment quanta directly.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Payments for adoption-related matters outside the permitted payment categories would be an offence.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Last, but not least, some Members raised queries on adoption-related issues not directly covered in the Bill.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng and Miss Rachel Ong asked if MSF will actively raise awareness and encourage adoption of children in state care.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng further asked if we would encourage respite fostering as an option for prospective adopters to determine their readiness for adoption.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Don Wee and Assoc Prof Jamus Lim asked about adoption leave.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Don Wee also asked about school fees for foreign stepchildren seeking to be adopted by their Singaporean parents.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Melvin Yong also requested for more information on MSF's efforts to encourage more to step forward to become foster parents and to provide them with additional childcare leave.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Dennis Tan suggested that the requirement for adopted children to take mandatory oaths of renunciation, allegiance and loyalty be dispensed with.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: An adoption order terminates the legal ties between a child and his or her birth parents and creates new ties between the child and his or her adoptive parents.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Given the gravity of an adoption order, it is crucial that the child is placed with adoptive parents who can provide a safe, stable and loving home for him or her.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This is done by clarifying the grounds under which the Court can dispense with birth parents' consent.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It is not in a child's welfare for him or her to linger in the state care system.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Adoption will give such children an opportunity to have a fresh start, experience stability and achieve better outcomes in life.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We must guard against any attempts to commoditise or exploit our children for financial or other gains.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Ultimately, this Bill will contribute to building strong families in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Like I said in my opening speech, families form the bedrock of our society.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: They are our foundation that nurtures and builds resilient individuals, providing the best source of safety, love and care for our children, so that they can learn, grow and lead meaningful and fulfilling lives.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Their valuable comments and suggestions have helped to shape and refine the proposals.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I would also like to thank prospective adopters and adoptive parents for opening your hearts and homes to the children who need them, so that they can have a good start in life and fulfil their potential.
